text:
support_jamie: FYI support alert - Pixelly reporting spikes of 503s for POST /v1/generate since ~10:03 UTC. Gateway shows upstream worker exits repeatedly. Request IDs: rQX1, rQX2, rQX5.

oncall_maya: :eyes: grabbing logs. Any recent config changes to batch/autotune?

support_jamie: Customer was using default autoscale + dynamic-batching. They reported turning on the workload optimizer (dynbatch) yesterday.

infra_ryan: I see worker pods crashing on the hosted infer fleet node group gc-hosted-3. Container exit code=137 then quick restart. Kernel logs show OOM killer invoked for process infer-runner.

eng_lee: Can you paste the runner stdout around the crash?

infra_ryan: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T10:02:14Z] infer-runner[pid=8421]: Allocating KV cache size=24MB seq=2048
[2026-03-17T10:03:01Z] infer-runner[pid=8421]: Batch alloc request tokens=8192 batch_size=8 -> attempting naive alloc
[2026-03-17T10:03:02Z] kernel: Memory cgroup: Killed process 8421 (infer-runner) total-vm:1024000kB, anon-rss:820000kB, oom_score_adj:0
[2026-03-17T10:03:02Z] containerd: container exited with status 137
```

support_jamie: Customer saw timeouts and UI retried which magnified QPS.

oncall_maya: Is this only Pixelly or global?

infra_ryan: Affected worker shards show a correlated ramp in allocated tokens per request; other tenants on same node group low impact. Looks like dynbatch created a much larger per-request allocation than expected for long prompts.

eng_lee: Repro plan: 1) run a local load test mimicking Pixelly payloads (large prompt + toolcall) 2) run with dynbatch on/off 3) monitor RSS and GPU allocation.

cust_ops_sam: Pixelly is on Dedicated trial but routed to hosted fallback when dedicated capacity saturated. They were hitting fallback during their peak. They asked for an incident summary for CS.

eng_lee: Short-term mitigation: disable dynbatch for the tenant routing, or pin to model-variant small-kv. Also add a circuit breaker to cap dynamic batch token allocations to 4096 tokens/request.

infra_ryan: I patched the autoscaler policy to opt-out Pixelly from dynbatch and increased eviction threshold on gc-hosted-3 to reduce noisy-neighbor reclamation. Restarted 3 pods in the shard.

deploybot: Deploy succeeded: autoscale-policy pixelly-optout @ gc-hosted-3 (rev 2026-03-17T10:10)

oncall_maya: After the restart we saw 503s drop to baseline within 2m. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.

support_jamie: Next steps (for postmortem): collect full coredumps from the worker nodes (if available), capture dynbatch decision logs, add an alert when per-request token allocation > 512kB, and update docs on dynbatch safe defaults.

eng_lee: Agreed. Also will add a regression test in perf-suite that simulates long-prompt toolcalls under dynbatch to catch this.

cust_ops_sam: I've notified Pixelly and offered a credit for the downtime; they'll want a write-up.

support_jamie: Thanks everyone. Marking incident resolved for now, keeping channel open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
